steps.text: A Cardiac Procedures nurse will call you 3 to 7 days before to go over your medicines and allergies.
If the Cardiac Procedures nurse hasn't called you yet, call the nurse coordinator at 206.598.8435 or 206.597.3609 (8 AM to 5 PM).
To reschedule or cancel, call 206.598.8200 right away.
Pack a small overnight bag in case you need to stay.
Arrange a responsible adult to drive you home. They must be with you in the Cardiac Procedures Unit before you leave. You can't take a bus, taxi or shuttle alone.
If you live out of town, think about booking a hotel nearby. Plan to spend most of the day at the hospital.
If you take warfarin (Coumadin), ask the provider who referred you whether and when to stop it.
If you take another blood thinner, the nurse will tell you whether it's OK to take.
If you take diabetes medicine, the dose may need to change. Ask the nurse.

Bring a list of all your medicines with doses (including vitamins and supplements), anything else you took in the last 2 days, the name and phone number of your contact person and your driver, your CPAP machine if you use one, and images from any earlier catheterization.
No caffeine: no coffee, tea, energy drinks, or supplements with caffeine.
No high-fat foods like bacon, sausage or eggs.
Stop eating and drinking now.
If you finish eating at least 6 hours before check-in, a light snack like tea and toast is fine. For a small meal, set an alarm for more than 8 hours before your procedure.
If you don't need any medicine changes, take your usual morning medicines with small sips of water. If your doctor prescribed aspirin for your heart, take it as usual that morning.
Check in at the Heart Institute, A-Wing, 1st floor.
After the procedure you'll rest in bed for 2 to 6 hours. You can eat as usual.
Don't take ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve, Naprosyn). They can cause bleeding. You can take acetaminophen (Tylenol).
For minor pain you can take Tylenol, 325 mg or 500 mg. Don't take more than 4,000 mg in 24 hours.
If your doctor prescribed aspirin for your heart, keep taking it as usual, but don't take extra aspirin for pain.
Restart all the heart medicines you took before. Keep taking your other medicines unless your doctor says otherwise.
Go back to your usual foods unless your doctor or nurse told you to change your diet.
You can take off the bandage 24 hours after your procedure. Then clean the site gently with mild soap and water and pat it dry.

For 3 days, watch the site. Call the cardiologist who did your procedure if you have redness, drainage, a fever over 101.5 F, a change in the bruise or lump, numbness in your arm or wrist (if the catheter went in your wrist), or bad pain that Tylenol doesn't help.
The site will likely be sore for 1 to 2 days. A bruise can take 2 to 3 weeks to fade, and after a groin site it may spread down your leg.

Sudden heavy bleeding or swelling you can't control: press firmly on the site and call 911. Light or moderate bleeding: press with clean fingers for 10 minutes; if it doesn't stop, call 911 and keep pressing. For an arm site, if the bleeding stops, sit quietly for 2 hours without bending the wrist and call the cardiologist.
Book a follow-up visit with your cardiologist or primary care provider, usually 2 to 4 weeks after you leave the hospital.

Weekdays 8 AM-5 PM, general questions: 206.598.8435 or 206.597.3609. Weekdays 6:30 AM-5 PM, questions about your procedure: 206.668.1085 (ask for a nurse). Urgent, after hours, weekends or holidays: 206.598.6190, ask to page the interventional cardiologist.
